title: Jaffa Cake Jaffa Cam Review
summary: Jaffa Cake made a camera for some reasons so I bought it
content:
As a novelty camera enjoyer, I had to get my hands on a Jaffa Cake Jaffa cam. Just look at it.

For a penny short of seven english pounds you get the camera, the keyring, a USB A to C cable (A, really?), and a pack of Jaffa Cakes. You do have to provide your own micro SD card.

On turning it on you get a little jingle and a Jaffa Cake splash screen. Cute. I stuck in a 1GB one I had lying around and it said I could fit around 7500 images on it which gives you some idea of how low quality these photos are going to be — or maybe McVities have cracked a new compression algorithm that will change the world? Sadly, it's the former. The photos are 1920×1440.

Each of these photos, along with the other ones I took, I was as steady as I could be and the light was decent. I'm starting to think these types of cameras exist purely to disprove "the best camera is the one you have with you". I reckon I could draw better representations of these moments.

The camera also has filters, which I didn't use for any photos worth sharing, including a santa one and a beach scene but no jaffa cake one. What are they even doing here? Useless.

Interestingly the B&M camera that Ben has appears to be more or less the exact same camera based on the UI and version number formatting. You shouldn't buy that one either.

The only conclusion to be drawn is that £7 isn't enough to get a good camera. The Jaffa Cakes were good though.
